newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare gains on Lozano firing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare gains on Lozano firing.

text.p: Mexican stocks rose Monday but ended off their highest levels of the day after Mexican Attorney General Antonio Lozano was fired, traders said.
The IPC index of blue-chip stocks rose 19.38 points to 3,311.07 after gaining about 34 points earlier in the session.

"It's crazy here," one trader said as the news broke about Lozano, who was the first opposition party member named to a cabinet post in decades. "People are putting in all kinds of sell orders out there."
"The news is not good and we'll have to wait and see if it is interpreted as a party political move ahed of (mid-term) elections in 1997," another trader said.
Volume was a sluggish 78 million shares. Of 103 stocks that traded, winners beat losers by 50 to 34. Blue chips were largely absent from the day's trading activity.
For most of the session, traders said stocks rallied as local and foreign bargain-hunters stepped in. Some also expected interest rates would fall.
Nonetheless, the Lozano news abruptly changed what had been a modestly optimistic market, they added.
"The news of changeover in the Attorney General's office definitely hit the market," said Roberto Solano, an analyst at the Estrategia Bursatil brokerage.
"The political background has held the bourse back, because economic fundamentals and technicals do favour a rally," he said.
